questions.question: What can you do in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it finishes before another vehicle arrives.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding on the shoulder or off the main road.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Use it only when it is cloudy.
Use it only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle fit you properly?

options.text: When you can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
When you can reach the controls by stretching.
When the handlebars are above your head.
When your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should also be able to reach and operate the controls easily.

questions.question: You drank alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Effects from drinking may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects from drinking may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your body. Your ability to ride and your judgment can still be affected.

questions.question: The body removes one drink of alcohol per hour. If someone drank 8 drinks 4 hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. If 8 drinks were consumed 4 hours ago, about 4 drinks remain in the body.

questions.question: What is the main active substance in marijuana?
questions.explanation: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main active substance in marijuana.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Riders often slow down by downshifting. Keep in mind that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you go fastest.
The one that lets you draft off other vehicles.
The one that helps other drivers see you.
The one in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps others see you and lets you see them. Avoid blind spots, wind blasts, and road hazards. Your position should make it clear the lane is yours and give you an escape route if danger appears. Choose a position with plenty of space around you.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle passengers?

options.text: Yes, only for passengers without their own license.

questions.explanation: Oregon law requires all motorcycle riders and passengers to wear a DOT-approved helmet.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: As part of your regular scanning routine.
Not helpful since you cannot do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Can long-term exposure to wind noise cause harm?

options.text: Yes, it can cause hearing loss.
No, it is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction for tires?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all more hazardous than dry pavement for motorcycles.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent crash injuries?

options.text: No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces crash injury risk. Choose a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. They should be made of sturdy material and fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required on motorcycles?
questions.explanation: Oregon requires motorcycles to have one to three white headlights, at least one red taillight, one white license plate light, at least one red brake light, amber turn signals (if built after 1972), a red rear reflector, at least one mirror, a horn, fenders on all wheels, at least one brake, and a working exhaust system. All lights must meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride after drinking. Do whatever is needed to stop them, including taking their keys if necessary. Help arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection, and how long does it take?

options.text: A few minutes, done once a month
A few minutes, done before every ride
Over an hour, done by a mechanic
Over an hour, only when carrying a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes, done before every ride
questions.explanation: Do a thorough pre-ride inspection before every ride. It should only take a few minutes.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce head or neck injury risk in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single best thing you can do to reduce head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: How can your body remove alcohol?
questions.explanation: Time is the only way your body can remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward with your arms slightly bent on the handle grips
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the handle grips
Lean over the bike with your arms holding you up
Keep your knees far from the gas tank

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward with your arms slightly bent on the handle grips
questions.explanation: Sit far enough forward so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handle grips. This lets you reach and control the motorcycle easily and comfortably.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects are stronger than when used alone
The effects are less dangerous than when used alone
The effects often cancel each other out

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than when used alone
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can impair your riding. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: How can you make sure other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if you need to.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist choose their lane position?

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Weave between different lane positions to keep other drivers away.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
Do not worry about lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position works for every situation. Move your position in the lane as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What best reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is the most important protection a rider can wear.

questions.question: When should reflective clothing be worn?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing at night to make yourself more visible. Bright colors with reflective material help other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and strong gloves.
